record_type: folder-level provenance record, compiled when the benchmark was merged into the package; NOT written at run time
scope: all files of the sub-folders forward, inverse, fenep and positivity that have no provenance record of their own (runs of 11 October 2026, UTC). Result files written by the drivers of this archive carry their own record under the key "provenance" (positivity/positivity.json, positivity/fenep_step.json) or in a file <name>.provenance.json (positivity/subordination_monte_carlo.json).
seed: recorded in every run file (key "seed"); data noise and initial guesses are derived from it as stated in code/configs/b5_inverse.json
configuration: the parameters of each run are recorded in its file (flow, Wi, Theta, alpha, frame, output map, residual norm, mesh size, iteration numbers); the remaining settings are those of code/configs/b5_forward.json, b5_inverse.json and b5_fenep.json, which are identical to the files used by the runs up to line endings

environment.source: not recorded by the runs: the environment of the machine on which they were made, as recorded by all other result files of this archive during the same hours and as found when this record was compiled; confirmed by the bit-for-bit repetition described under "verification"

timestamps: modification time (UTC) of each result file, listed under "files"; first and last per sub-folder under "run_period_utc"
workers: at most three worker processes with one torch thread each; wall times in the files were measured on a machine shared with other jobs

source_at_run_time.note: sha256 (16 hex digits, line endings normalised) of the sources that produced the files; the package modules were a frozen copy of fracsp taken on 2026-10-11T18:26:22Z

source_in_archive.note: the same sources after the merge: spd.py became the module fracsp.spd and imports the package modules of the archive; the drivers write to results/raw/B5_conformation and add a provenance record; b5_positivity.py also writes the Monte Carlo record subordination_monte_carlo.json. Fingerprints of the present files; see "revisions" for the changes since the merge

verification.note: a subset was recomputed with the sources of the archive on the same machine and compared value by value with the stored files (wall-time fields excluded): all 24 stepper baselines and 12 exact references of the forward benchmark, 12 forward training runs (every output map / residual norm, both flows, both frames, both orders, seeds 0-4) and one run with the three-fold budget, the 4 FENE-P references and stepper baselines and 7 FENE-P training runs (every variant), 4 inverse training runs, 6 least-squares fits, the Cramer-Rao bounds, and the three files of the sub-folder positivity

revisions.change: fracsp.spd: the implicit L1 step of the nonlinear laws has exactly one admissible solution for every step size; new functions fenep_step_root and giesekus_step_root return it, and solve_l1 accepts the result of Newton's iteration only if it is admissible (argument nonlinear='safeguarded', the default; 'newton' is the plain iteration used before, also available as solve_l1_newton; 'root' solves every step by the root solver). The arithmetic of Newton's iteration is unchanged. b5_positivity.py runs the plain Newton iteration and the safeguarded solver for the nonlinear laws; b5_fenep_step.py is new; the docstring of b5_fenep.py was extended.
files_regenerated: positivity/positivity.json (the values of all keys of the earlier file are reproduced exactly; keys safeguarded_* and step_condition_lhs added)
revisions.stored_results_checked: all other files are unchanged. The references (graded meshes with 2048 and 4096 steps), the stepper baselines (128 steps) and the a-priori scales (64 steps) of the FENE-P benchmark were computed with the plain Newton iteration; b5_fenep_step.py recomputes them: the Newton iterates are admissible at every step, the safeguarded solver returns bit-identical arrays, and the root solver agrees with them to a relative difference of at most 2.1e-14 (stored reference files: 4.5e-14); see tables/data/Table_B5_fenep_stored_check.csv. The linear law (forward and inverse benchmarks) is not affected: its step is linear.

revisions.change: fracsp.spd: new variant nonlinear='newton-full' of solve_l1, Newton's iteration with full steps (also solve_l1_newton(..., full=True)). The variant 'newton', called the plain iteration in the entry above, halves a step of the FENE-P law as long as the new iterate would have tr C >= b, and is now documented as such; its arithmetic and that of 'safeguarded' and 'root' are unchanged. A step at which Newton's iteration does not converge raises a RuntimeError with the attributes step and iterates. b5_fenep_step.py runs both Newton variants on every mesh, records the parameters of the iteration (key newton_iteration) and a second case study (key case2: Wi = 20, alpha = 0.9, b = 10, 512 uniform steps, a mesh within the step bound of the linear law on which the iteration with full steps passes the pole tr C = b at step 9). b5_positivity.py: wording of the docstring, comments and printed lines only.
files_regenerated: positivity/fenep_step.json (every value of the earlier file is reproduced exactly: runs and summaries of both sweeps, case study, check of the stored files; new keys newton_full_*, newton_iteration and case2)
revisions.stored_results_checked: all other files are unchanged, and the functions that produced them were not modified. In the entry above, 'plain Newton iteration' means the variant 'newton' (steps halved at the pole tr C = b): the references, stepper baselines and a-priori scales of the FENE-P benchmark were computed with it, and tables/data/Table_B5_fenep_stored_check.csv, which recomputes them, is regenerated identically.
